# Eosinophilic lung diseases

*Categories: Clinical knowledge > Internal medicine > Pulmonology > Other pulmonologic disorders > Eosinophilic lung diseases*

[Original Article Link](/library/cu0aJ3)

---

## Summary

Eosinophilic <u>lung</u> diseases encompass a spectrum of pulmonary conditions characterized by pulmonary and/or peripheral <u>eosinophilia</u>. These disorders may be <u>idiopathic</u> or secondary to etiologies such as <u>helminth infections</u>, pharmacological agents, or environmental triggers. Diagnostic workup generally includes clinical evaluation, imaging studies, <u>bronchoalveolar lavage</u> (<u>BAL</u>), and occasionally <u>lung</u> <u>biopsy</u> to confirm pulmonary <u>eosinophilia</u> and exclude differential diagnoses. Eosinophilic pneumonias are a type of eosinophilic <u>lung</u> disease characterized by significant infiltration of <u>eosinophils</u> in the <u>alveoli</u> and pulmonary <u>interstitium</u>. <u>Simple pulmonary eosinophilia</u> (<u>Loeffler syndrome</u>) is characterized by transient migratory <u>pulmonary consolidations</u> on imaging with peripheral <u>eosinophilia</u> that typically resolves spontaneously within a month. <u>Acute idiopathic eosinophilic pneumonia</u> is a rapidly progressive eosinophilic pulmonary condition that may lead to <u>hypoxemic respiratory failure</u>, often precipitated by recent exposure to inhaled irritants such as <u>tobacco smoke</u> or dust. <u>Acute idiopathic eosinophilic pneumonia</u> manifests with bilateral reticular opacities and <u>pleural effusions</u> and rapidly improves with a short course of high-dose IV <u>glucocorticoids</u>. <u>Chronic eosinophilic pneumonia</u> is an insidious eosinophilic <u>lung</u> disorder of unknown cause commonly associated with <u>atopic</u> conditions such as <u>asthma</u> or <u>eczema</u>. <u>Chronic eosinophilic pneumonia</u> is characterized by peripheral and predominantly upper lobe consolidations and often requires prolonged <u>glucocorticoid</u> therapy due to a high risk of recurrence.
